question: Blend photographs of 32 faces into one average face. How do people rate its attractiveness against the originals?
answer: Higher than most. Langlois and Roggman found such composites rated above nearly all the faces in them. Averaging smooths blemishes, evens out asymmetry and makes something that looks familiar. In an ancient story, the painter Zeuxis built Helen from the best features of five women.
move: Familiar and smooth can feel like beautiful; ask which you are judging.
ask: Do I like this face, song or idea because it is good, or because it feels familiar?
trap: Duller, because an average face should look bland.
reference: Judith H. Langlois & Lori A. Roggman, Attractive faces are only average, Psychological Science, 1990
